The incidence differential has an identity free block and a rank-s block of coordinate combinations. In characteristic zero independent differentials imply algebraic independence. Maximal-coefficient reduction then gives exact Gauss values for every coefficient polynomial. Thus the SAME complete full coefficient-Gauss field F embeds isometrically into every H'_i. notes.text:
For normalized actual E1 u set B=-E_theta(u)>=0 and A_mu=int(-u)dmu. Let U=sup_{B<=1,sup u=0}A_mu and J=sup_continuous(E-int u), with mu(T)=RAW V.

All-test integrability implies finite U without a common anchor. Otherwise choose costs<=1 and A(u_j)>=4^j. Actual convex sums w_N=sum_{j<=N}2^-j u_j+2^-N0 decrease with E>=-1. Extended energy applies BEFORE E1 membership. An identically-minus-infinity endpoint would, by compact closed superlevels, put a tail below every constant -R and force energy<=-RV, a contradiction. O's decreasing energy then makes the actual nontrivial endpoint E1. SEQUENTIAL monotone convergence gives integral at least sum2^j=infinity. Conversely B(tu)<=tB(u), with t=min(1,1/B)>0, proves every test integrable from finite U. Finite constant shifts give absolute integrability.

Finite continuous J implies all-test integrability. For continuous actual majorants v_lambda decreasing to E1 u, a tail has finite upper bound R and int(R-v_lambda)<=RV+J-E(u). The necessary Radon-net law holds for increasing nonnegative continuous/lsc functions: strict open levels are directed unions; compact inner approximations have finite subcovers; one common stage approximates any finite lower layer sum. Height truncation and layer refinement yield endpoint integral=sup stage integrals. Arbitrary measurable-net convergence is not assumed. The finite bound excludes infinity and proves integral convergence. O's energy law then gives equality of continuous and all-E1 dual suprema.

With n3's moment, O makes A_k=int(-u)MA(u^[k],0^[n-k]) finite nonnegative, sum A_k=(n+1)B and A0<=M0. Actual affine curvature and segment differentiation give, for ALL real 0<=t<=1,
B(tu)=sum_k binom(n,k)A_k integral_0^t s^k(1-s)^(n-k)ds.
The k0 term is at most tM0; positive Bernstein weights sum to1-(1-s)^n<=ns. Thus B(tu)<=tM0+D_n t^2 B, where D_n=n(n+1)/2.

IF U IS FINITE, choose t=(1+2M0+sqrt(2D_nB))^-1. Its cost is at most one, so tA<=U. Consequently
A_mu(u)<=U[1+2M0+sqrt(2D_nB)],
F_mu(u)<=-B+U(1+2M0)+U sqrt(2D_nB),
J<=U(1+2M0)+D_n U^2/2.
This proves the converse finite-dual implication and coercivity for the explicitly quantified finite targets. Reference covariance makes the absolute criterion intrinsic. No support restriction, probability normalization or subtraction of infinite values is used.

The omitted hypothesis is MATERIAL. On actual P1/O(1) with Gauss theta, N gives M0=0. Choose 0<|a|<1 and ell_m=-m log|a|. Generating sections T1,a^mT0 give continuous FS u_m=logmax(|z|,exp(-ell))-logmax(1,|z|), supremum zero. Q gives genuine curvature delta at the shrinking-disk Gauss point, and O gives E=-ell/2. For raw-mass-one target delta_(z=0), B=ell/2 but F=ell/2 tends to PLUS infinity. Scaling t=ell^-1/2 gives B=1/2 and A=sqrt ell, hence U=infinity. Therefore M0 alone cannot imply coercivity.
